title: Cost-aware routing: GPU selection & spot/on-demand budget caps
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Goal: Implement policy-driven routing that selects between spot and on-demand capacity and chooses GPU types based on cost/latency trade-offs, with per-customer daily and monthly budget caps and graceful fallback to cheaper model variants when budgets are hit.

Background: We already have smart routing primitives (region/tier routing, model variant fallbacks) but lack fine-grained cost-aware controls: (1) automated preference for spot capacity where acceptable, (2) GPU selection rules (H100 vs A100 vs T4) driven by request class / cost target, and (3) per-customer budget caps that throttle or downgrade requests rather than causing hard failures. This ticket covers design, runtime policy engine changes, and a canary rollout.

Scope:
- Policy language additions: budget caps (soft/hard), spot-preference thresholds, GPU-type preference with fallback ordering, model-variant downgrade rules.
- Runtime router changes to evaluate cost-score = f(latency_sensitivity, cost_target, historical spot stability) and select node pool.
- Billing hook to increment budget counters and surface near-limit alerts in Console.
- Fallback behaviors: degrade to quantized / smaller model variant or switch from spot -> on-demand when reliability drops or budget exceeded.
- Tests: unit, integration in staging with synthetic workloads simulating spot preemption and GPU availability variance.

Success metrics:
- 20% reduction in average per-token serving cost for non-latency-critical workloads in pilot customers.
- <1% increase in tail latency (p99) for latency-sensitive tiers after canary.
- No customer-visible 5xx increase in rollout phase.

Non-goals: pricing changes, billing reconciliation backend replacement, or end-user UI polishing (Console alerts basic only for rollout).
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema extended and validated in CI: budget_caps, spot_preference, gpu_priority_list, downgrade_rules
Router evaluates cost-score and selects node pools deterministically given same inputs
Budget enforcement implemented with soft-warning at 90% and controlled downgrade at 100% for soft caps; hard caps return configured fallback behavior
Canary run (10% traffic) for 2 weeks with metrics dashboard: cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, spot preemption rate
Integration tests simulate spot preemption and GPU pool exhaustion with deterministic fallback to on-demand or smaller variant
Docs: PRD and runtime policy reference published (Confluence) and Console shows basic budget burn rate for canary customers
notes: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff: aligned with PM on project goals and success metrics. Action: design policy DSL prototype. (Ava)

2025-02-18 - Design review: decided on explicit gpu_priority_list (e.g., [H100, A100, T4]) per route instead of inferred mapping. Trade-off: simpler policy vs more config surface. Approve: PM + Infra leads.

2025-02-21 - Prototype router change committed (internal branch). Key change: calculate cost_score = alpha*cost_estimate + beta*latency_penalty + gamma*spot_stability. Defaults set to favor spot when cost savings > 35% and latency_sensitivity == low.

2025-02-24 - Security review: no secret or KMS change required; budget counters stored in existing metering table. Security note: ensure rate of budget-check queries cannot be abused. (Security team sign-off pending low-risk)
2025-02-26 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5432 — router: cost-aware selection + gpu_priority_list parsing. Needs tests and load-testing results before merge. (Rishi)

2025-02-27 - Integration tests: added spot preemption simulation harness. Observed that naive immediate switch to on-demand causes brief latency spikes; we added a short retry-backoff window and switch-on-failure after 3 preemptions in 60s.
2025-02-28 - PM requested budget UX: Console will show "near cap" email and webhook at 80% of soft cap. Work scoped as follow-up but basic webhook added for canary customers.

2025-03-01 - Ready for canary: create routing policies for pilot accounts (acme-analytics, beta-startup). Canary config: 10% traffic, 4-week window, metrics dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/routing/ENG-9573-canary
